label: Additional Mechanical Models
notes: This appendix is a gallery, not a single theorem. Each model is chosen because it lets the geometric machinery of the book show its strength: symmetry produces conserved quantities, conserved quantities permit reduction, and reduction often exposes hidden action-angle structure. We tour seven worked examples and read each as integrable geometry.

label: Reading an Integrable Model
notes: Set the common vocabulary first. A symmetry is a group action preserving the Hamiltonian; Noether converts it to a momentum map; level sets of commuting integrals foliate phase space; on compact regular leaves Liouville-Arnold gives tori and angle coordinates. Every example below is one instance of this single pipeline.

label: Spherical Pendulum
notes: The spherical pendulum is the cleanest case. A point mass on a sphere under gravity has rotational symmetry about the vertical, so the azimuthal momentum is conserved. Eliminating the angle leaves a one-dimensional problem in the polar angle governed by an effective potential with a centrifugal barrier.

label: Effective Potential and Turning Latitudes
notes: Here we read the reduced radial picture. The effective potential combines gravity with the centrifugal term from the conserved azimuthal momentum. Energy is a horizontal line; its two intersections with the potential are the turning latitudes. The mass oscillates in latitude between them while precessing in longitude, tracing a band on the sphere.

label: The Three Classical Tops
notes: Rigid body rotation about a fixed point is integrable in exactly three classical cases. Euler: no gravity, motion by inertia alone. Lagrange: a symmetric top with center of mass on the symmetry axis. Kovalevskaya: a special inertia ratio two-to-two-to-one with the center of mass in the equatorial plane. Each adds one subtle integral.

label: The Lagrange Top
notes: The Lagrange top is the spinning toy gyroscope. Axial symmetry gives two conserved momenta about the vertical and the figure axis, and energy is the third integral. Reduction to the nutation angle yields an effective potential, so the axis nutates between two cones while precessing, exactly mirroring the spherical pendulum structure.

label: The Kovalevskaya Top
notes: Kovalevskaya found the last integrable top by demanding the solution be meromorphic in complex time. Her extra integral is quartic in the momenta, not quadratic, and was invisible to physical intuition. It is the historical proof that integrability can be a deep analytic property, discoverable only through careful global structure.

label: Geodesics and Billiards in an Ellipse
notes: Confocal conics drive this example. A geodesic on an ellipsoid, or a billiard inside an ellipse, conserves a second quantity beyond energy: every segment stays tangent to one fixed confocal conic, the caustic. That caustic is the integral made visible, and elliptic coordinates separate the motion completely.

label: The Toda Lattice
notes: The Toda lattice is a chain of particles with exponential nearest-neighbour springs. It is an integrable many-body system: written in Lax pair form, the eigenvalues of the Lax matrix are conserved under the flow. This isospectral structure produced solitons and seeded the modern theory of integrable systems.

label: Point Vortices in the Plane
notes: Point vortices turn fluid dynamics into a finite Hamiltonian system. Vortex positions are conjugate variables weighted by circulation, and the Hamiltonian is the logarithmic interaction energy. Translational and rotational symmetry give conserved linear and angular impulse, making two and three vortex problems integrable and four generically chaotic.

label: Ideal Fluid as Geodesics
notes: Arnold's deepest reframing closes the gallery. The Euler equations of an incompressible ideal fluid are exactly the geodesic equations on the infinite-dimensional group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms, with the kinetic-energy metric. Fluid motion is free motion, and the curvature of that group controls predictability of the flow.

label: Synthesis
notes: Step back and see the single idea. Across pendulum, tops, billiards, lattices, vortices and fluids, the same geometric reflex applies: find the symmetry, build the momentum map, reduce, and look for the tori. The models differ in dimension and difficulty but share one grammar of integrable mechanics.
